Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 24850 of 2023

Applicant :- Virendra Singh And Another
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Nitinjay Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sanjeev Kumar Pandey

Hon'ble Gajendra Kumar,J.
Heard Sri Nitinjay Pandey, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Sanjeev Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 as well as learned AGA for the State.

The present application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants with the prayer to quash the impugned judgement and order dated 23.06.2023 passed by Judicial Magistrate, Etah in Criminal Case No.2034 of 2018, arising out of Case Crime No.168 of 2017, under Sections 120-B, 419, 420 IPC, Police station Rijor, District Etah.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicants are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is further submitted that no case is made out for the aforesaid offences against the applicants.
Further submission is that complainant in order to harass with malicious intention made false complaint against the applicants.

Further submission is that the ground, which has been taken by the applicants in their discharge application has not been looked Virendra Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157395008/
1 into by the court below.

entities.text: Virendra Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the impugned order was passed by the concerned Magistrate without application of mind and the same is nothing but an abuse of process of law.
On the other hand, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 have opposed the prayer and submitted that there is no illegality in the impugned order.
A prima facie case is made out against the applicants.
Counsel for the appellants has not been able to point out any such illegality much less than any abuse of court's process which may persuade this Court to interfere in the impugned order.
The impugned order reflects judicial application of mind.
There appears no good ground to castigate the impugned order.
The view taken by the court below seems to be correct and even this Court does not have reason to take a different view in the matter.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, after perusing the impugned order as well as the materials brought on record and having considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, I do not find any good ground to quash the impugned order.
Hence, the prayer made in the application is refused.
With the aforesaid observations, the present application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is dismissed.
